question: How often is this changelog reviewed and extended?
options: Whenever a vendor announces a new model
Quarterly: the status boxes are checked against primary sources and a new section is added
Once a year
Never: the changelog is fixed when the track ships
explanation: A fixed quarterly cadence keeps the volatile edge current without chasing every announcement. The October 2026 survey is the current one; January 2027 is next.

question: Which MCP change from July 2026 affects the server you built in module 03 and reused in the capstone?
options: MCP was replaced by A2A
Revision 2026-07-28 made requests stateless, with the protocol version in `_meta` on every request and `server/discover` instead of the `initialize` handshake
MCP dropped JSON-RPC for gRPC
MCP servers can no longer expose tools
explanation: The 2026-07-28 revision removed the handshake and session state; many deployed servers still speak 2025-11-25, so check what your SDK supports.

question: What did the Digital Omnibus on AI, in force since 27 July 2026, change?
options: It repealed the EU AI Act
It moved the EU AI Act's high-risk obligations to 2 December 2027 (Annex III) and 2 August 2028 (Annex I)
It banned general-purpose models in the EU
It only applies to Brazil
explanation: The Omnibus amended the application dates of high-risk obligations. Transparency duties still applied from 2 August 2026, with a grace period for marking content from existing generative systems.

question: A change earns a line in the changelog when it...
options: was covered by many news sites
changes what an engineer should do or know in one of the track's modules, dated by the event itself
comes from the largest vendor
includes a new benchmark record
explanation: The changelog tracks consequences for practice, with the date of the specification, release or legal event, not the date of the coverage.

question: Looking at a year of changes in the table, which statement holds?
options: Every change invalidated the track's core rules

Names, versions, dates and defaults changed, but core rules held: injection is solved by architecture rather than prompts, evals beat impressions, workflows come before agents, loops need budgets and verifiers
Nothing changed in the field
Prompt injection was solved in 2026
explanation: This is why the track separates the stable core from the volatile edge: the edge moves monthly, the core decides how you build.

question: How can you apply the changelog idea to your own production AI system?
options: Use the latest model alias so you never need to track changes
Keep a dated changelog of your dependencies (model snapshots, protocol revisions, SDK versions, policies) and review it on a fixed cadence
Rely on vendor emails
Only track changes after an incident
explanation: Most surprises come from an undocumented dated change: a retired snapshot, a new protocol revision, a changed default. Writing them down and reviewing them makes them planned work.
